title: Prepare a lesson
question:
Here is a five-minute idea to get bodies and minds moving before the lesson:

1. Brief stretching (1 min)
• Stand up, reach your arms up and take deep breaths.
• Lean your torso to each side.
2. “Simon says” with movement (2 min)
• “Simon says: jump on the spot, touch your knees, turn all the way around.”
• Change the instructions quickly to keep the pace.
3. Mini circuit (1 min)
• 30 seconds of gentle jumps.
• 30 seconds of heel kicks.
4. An energetic finish (1 min)
• Clap a rhythm while counting aloud to eight.
• Finish with a group cheer.
Do you like it, or would you prefer another idea?
source: Source: PROFE GABI textos · M01, M03, M04 · English translation of exhibition adaptation

follow.label: A lesson on separating mixtures
follow.user: Design a playful, dynamic lesson for seventh grade on separating mixtures by decantation and distillation. Include the objective, opening, main activities and a metacognitive closing.
follow.gabi:
Objective: investigate decantation and distillation to separate mixtures and explain how each method works.

Opening (10 min): present water with oil and salt water. Ask pairs how they would separate each mixture and collect their ideas.

Main activities (35 min): the proposal includes decantation (15 min) and distillation (20 min), with observation and a record of what students learned.

Metacognitive closing (10 min): what did we learn about each method? Where could we use them in daily life? Complete: “What surprised me most was…”

provenance.responseTreatment: English translation of the Spanish exhibition draft

follow.label: Movement skills in first grade
follow.user: Can you plan a first-grade lesson on basic movement skills, including the lesson objective, curriculum objectives, indicators, opening, main activities, closing, assessment and resources?
follow.gabi:
Here is a short first-grade plan for basic movement skills:

Objective: demonstrate and control movement and balance.

Opening (5 min): “Simon says”. Main activities (20 min): jumping and balance stations, plus a cone circuit. Closing (5 min): which skill did you enjoy most, and why?

Formative assessment: use a checklist at the stations and a brief oral self-assessment at the end. Resources: hoops or chalk, tape, cones or plastic bottles, and a clock.

title: Create activities and assess
question:
Here is a worksheet for paired work in Biology Unit 1:

1. Reading comprehension
“Living things carry out functions such as nutrition, interaction and reproduction. These help them maintain internal balance (homeostasis) and adapt to their environment.”
What functions do living things perform? What is homeostasis for?

2. Multiple choice: identify what homeostasis means.
3. Matching terms: connect nutrition, reproduction and homeostasis with their definitions.
4. Complete sentences about the functions of living things.

follow.label: When to use summative assessment
follow.user: Can I start a unit and give a summative assessment on the same day?
follow.gabi:
Hello! Summative assessment measures achievement at the end of a unit, after teaching and formative feedback.

If you start the unit and give a summative assessment on the same day, students will not have had time to practise or use feedback.

I suggest:
• Plan formative activities such as rubrics, peer assessment and self-assessment.
• Give feedback throughout the unit.
• Schedule summative assessment at the end, once the learning objectives have been met.

provenance.responseTreatment: English translation of the Spanish exhibition draft

follow.take: Assessment is planned alongside teaching and feedback.

follow.label: A rubric for Music
follow.user: Help me create suitable rubric criteria for second-grade Music students learning a song on a metallophone or recorder.
follow.gabi:
I suggest four criteria with four achievement levels: 4—Excellent; 3—Good; 2—Acceptable; 1—Needs support.

1. Rhythm and tuning
2. Instrumental technique
3. Expression and dynamics
4. Responsibility and care

For example, in responsibility and care, level 4 describes a student who always prepares, puts away and cares for the instrument; level 2 means the student needs frequent reminders.

title: Look after my wellbeing
question:
I understand how you feel. Balancing marking and personal time is a real challenge.

Here are some ideas:
• Set marking blocks: spend 30–45 minutes a day marking, then stop.
• Prioritise: identify which assignments need detailed feedback and which can receive general comments.
• Use clear rubrics: they save time and show students what is expected.
• Share the workload: consider peer assessment with colleagues or exchanging tests.

And remember to look after yourself:
1. Set time limits and keep to them.
2. Schedule short breaks to recharge.
3. Protect real time to switch off at the weekend.
source: Source: PROFE GABI textos · M08, M07 · English translation of exhibition adaptation

follow.label: Help my class stay focused
follow.user: Act as a classroom climate expert. I need a focus strategy for ninth grade: students are easily distracted and talk a lot.
follow.gabi:
Here is a simple plan for ninth grade:

1. Attention signal
• Agree on a sound or gesture, such as “1-2-3, eyes on me”. Practise it two or three times at the start.
2. Short, clear work periods
• Divide activities into five- to ten-minute blocks. Use a visible timer.
3. Group roles
• Make teams of three or four. Assign a “focus keeper” to help the group stay on task.
4. Active breaks
• Every 15–20 minutes, take one or two minutes to stretch or breathe.
5. Positive reinforcement
• Praise students who help the class refocus. Simple incentives such as applause or stickers can help.
